title: introduce-snapshot-resolver-and-staged-retries-cross-sdk-ergonomics-bump
author: Amina Shah
release_notes: Adds a SnapshotResolver abstraction for deterministic session snapshots, introduces 'staged' retry presets for lower-latency fast-fail behavior, and bumps Python/TS/Go SDK minor versions to align ergonomics and docs. No public API breaking changes expected; some internal session types were stabilized.
description:
Motivation: Customers building replication and replay systems asked for a deterministic way to capture/restore session state across restarts and to pre-warm credentials for short-lived tokens. This PR adds a lightweight SnapshotResolver abstraction (pluggable per-SDK) plus a 'staged' retry profile that aggressively fast-fails on transient auth errors while preserving a longer fallback profile for backend retries. The change spans py/ts/go SDKs and the redwood SDK bridge to keep cross-language ergonomics consistent.

What I changed (summary): - Introduced SnapshotResolver interface and reference implementations (memory + file-backed) in each SDK. - Added staged retry presets: fast-fail -> short backoff -> fallback policy. - Plumbed SnapshotResolver through session creation (optional param) so server-side mgrs can persist snapshots. - Improved generator/async iterator ergonomics in TS/Py: explicit close() and resume_from_snapshot() helpers. - Go: added typed iterator safety wrappers and idempotent resume helper. - Centralized small docstrings/README snippets to show cross-SDK examples. - Minor version bumps: py-sdk 1.9.0 -> 1.10.0, ts-sdk 2.4.3 -> 2.5.0, go-sdk v0.8.7 -> v0.9.0.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear linked (ENG-3092) - [x] Unit tests added for resolver behavior and retry composition - [x] End-to-end smoke test in benchmark-lab to validate resume semantics - [x] Updated SDK READMEs with examples - [x] Version bumps and changelogs updated

Notes: This is intended to be non-breaking for existing users: SnapshotResolver is optional and default behavior preserves current in-memory session semantics. The staged retry presets are additive; existing retry profiles remain available. For pinned customers we will coordinate the minor SDK bumps with the respective account owners.
commits: 6 commits: 1) add snapshot resolver spec and tests; 2) implement py memory+file resolver; 3) implement ts resolver and async iterator helpers; 4) implement go iterator resume helpers and safety wrappers; 5) add staged retry presets + shared retry composer; 6) bump versions, update changelogs and README examples.
review_thread:
Diego: Can you clarify why the file-backed implementation chooses JSON.gz instead of protobuf?
Amina: JSON.gz was chosen for readability during debug and to avoid adding proto deps to reference impl; we can provide a proto-backed example in a follow-up if needed.

Priya: TS API ergonomics look good, but the close()/resume_from_snapshot() names feel ad-hoc vs existing Stream.close() naming. Could we align names?
Amina: Renamed stream.close() -> closeStream() in the TS helper and added deprecation note for the alias to keep ergonomics consistent.

Ethan: Tests flaked on CI (py flaky test_snapshot_resolver_timeout).
Amina: Root cause was a timing assumption; switched to a deterministic fake clock in tests and added a retry window. Reran CI and tests passed.

Diego: Approval pending small docs nit about error codes returned by staged retry.
Amina: Addressed - clarified mapping and added example table in docs. Diego approved on 2026-02-22. Priya approved on 2026-02-22. Ethan approved after rerun on 2026-02-23.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: unit(py) failed (flaky timing) -> fix applied; subsequent CI: all checks pass. Matrix: py 3.10/3.11/3.12, ts node 18/20, go 1.20 passed. Lint: ok. Bench smoke: ok. Security scan: no findings.
merge_outcome: merged (squash) on 2026-02-23 by Diego Ramos; merge commit summarizes snapshot resolver + staged retries + SDK bumps
post_merge_tasks: Publish SDK releases for Py/TS/Go (Amina + release-engineer), notify enterprise customers pinned to SDK versions, schedule a follow-up to add proto-backed snapshot impl for heavy customers.
notes_for_backport: No backport required; if backporting to release/* for critical customers, ensure the staged retry presets are gated behind a feature flag to avoid changing default behavior.
security_considerations: Snapshot files may contain transient auth tokens if customers choose to persist entire session context. The docs include a note recommending redaction and use of KMS for file-backed persistence. No secrets are persisted by default in the provided examples.
footprint_estimate: Medium: cross-SDK changes + tests + docs. Estimated runway for reviewers: 3-4 engineer-days to fully vet for enterprise customers.
